title: Five Eyes Agencies Urge Faster Cyber Preparedness for Frontier AI
key_facts: New Zealand's National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC) joined other Five Eyes cyber security agencies in urging organisations to strengthen cyber preparedness as frontier AI changes the pace and scale of digital threats.

The joint call to action was issued on 23 June 2026; it warns that frontier AI systems enable faster identification and exploitation of vulnerabilities while also creating chances to improve cyber defence.
Catriona Robinson, Deputy Director General Cyber Security and head of the NZ NCSC, endorsed the statement.
Organisations should understand their cyber risk exposure, strengthen foundational security controls and make sure cyber security leaders have enough authority and resources.

The NCSC is developing a programme of work, working with frontier AI model providers to assess emerging risks, and has published guidance on vulnerability management and cyber readiness in the frontier AI era.
Robinson said breaches will occur but preparedness helps contain them quickly and prevent escalation into major operational and financial crises.

why_it_matters_hint: Government cyber agencies in the Five Eyes alliance tell organisations to expect faster AI-driven attacks and to plan how to contain breaches.
